transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... well, I suppose I'm here because... I've been having some trouble staying in my chair. During staff meetings at school, or even just at dinner. 

I just... I keep getting up when everyone else is seated. Like I'll suddenly decide I need to refill my coffee, or walk to the back of the room to check a handout. Even when nothing is really urgent. So... yes, that's what brought me in.
Do you feel anxious or nervous when you're seated in those meetings or at dinner?
No... I don't think so. It's not really nerves. I just... I don't know, I just find myself standing up.
Do you feel like you have to get up and move around when you're seated?

I don't really know. I suppose... maybe a little? I haven't really thought about it like that. I just... I guess it's just hard to stay still for too long. It's not something I really dwell on, I just find myself doing it.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions over and over, like checking or arranging things?
No... I don't think so. I don't really arrange things or... check things. It's just what I mentioned before.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're trying to stay still?

I suppose so... When I'm sitting at my desk grading essays, or... at church, maybe. I just catch myself tapping my foot. Or clicking my pen. Just shifting around a bit. I usually have to... remind myself to settle down.
Do you feel restless or fidgety in most situations where you have to stay still?
I don't know about most situations... no. Um... probably just the ones I brought up. I haven't really noticed it beyond that.
When did you first notice yourself having trouble staying still in situations like meetings or dinner?

I suppose... it's been a long time. Even as a girl, um... my report cards usually said I was bright, but that I couldn't stay in my seat. Or wait my turn. My mother used to joke that I... well, that I wore a path between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was ten. So... I guess it isn't exactly new.
Has your difficulty staying still caused any problems for you at work or in your relationships?

I... suppose it does. A little. Um... mostly just people losing patience with me. In staff meetings at work, or... my book club. It's... well, you go to those things to connect with people, and I usually just leave feeling rather embarrassed instead. So... yes.
Have you experienced this difficulty staying still consistently throughout your life?

I... I'm not really sure. Um... I haven't exactly kept a record of it over the years. I suppose I just... I haven't really thought about whether it was happening every single year. So... I don't know.
Did you have trouble staying still when you were a little girl, like in elementary school?

I... well, yes. I believe I mentioned that just a few minutes ago. Um... about my old report cards. They always noted that I was bright, but that I just couldn't stay in my seat... or wait my turn. And that joke my mother used to make, about me wearing a path in the floor to the pencil sharpener... that was all before I was ten. So... yes. It was happening back then.
Do you feel guilty or anxious when you try to remain seated and find yourself unable to do so?

I... I wouldn't say I feel anxious, exactly. Um... or guilty. I suppose I just... I don't really dwell on the emotional side of it. If I can't sit, I... well, I just get up. I haven't really thought about it much beyond that.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted or having trouble paying attention?
I... no, I don't think so. Um... I haven't really noticed any problems with that. I can focus on things just fine.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?
I... well, I suppose everyone does that sometimes. But... no, I wouldn't say I do it often. I generally try to be careful.
How old were you when you first started noticing that you couldn't stay still?

I... I'm not sure of an exact age. Um... a long time ago. Even as a girl, I suppose. 

My mother used to joke that I... well, that I wore a path between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was ten. And... my old report cards usually said I was bright but couldn't stay in my seat, or... wait my turn. I just... I was an active child, I suppose.
Do you often forget things you were supposed to do?
I... no, not really. Um... I manage my classes and grading well enough, so... I make sure things get done. No, I wouldn't say that's a problem for me.
Has this difficulty staying still been present for at least 6 months?

I... yes, I suppose it has. Um... maybe for about eight months or so. It's... well, it's just been noticeably harder to manage lately. My youngest left for college around then, and... the house became much quieter. So... yes, I suppose it's been at least that long.
Has this difficulty staying still been a persistent issue throughout your adult life as well, not just in the last 8 months?
I... well, I suppose it's always been there, in the background. It just... wasn't as obvious when I had three children running around and a full house to manage. So... yes, I suppose it has been.
Has this difficulty staying still been present in some form since childhood, or did it start later in life?

I... yes, I suppose it goes back that far. Um... even as a girl, my report cards would say I was bright, but... that I couldn't stay in my seat, or wait my turn. My mother... well, she used to joke that I wore a path between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was ten. So... yes. It started early.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or activities?
I... no, I don't think so. I've been a teacher for a long time, so... organizing things is just part of the job. I manage that fine.
